Tessa / team — I started the initial checks and here's what I have so far (quick triage):

What I checked (now):
- Autoscaler: no unusual scale-down events in the cluster; node counts steady.
- Queue lengths (frontend): a spike in tokenization queue wait times at ~08:56.
- KV cache: elevated local eviction rates on two hosts pinned to bc-prod-1 nodepool.
- Recent deploys: none in the last 2 hours.

Immediate mitigations I can run in the next 10–15 minutes (need owner/approval):
A) Rebalance traffic away from bc-prod-1 nodepool -> will require short re-route (risk: transient p50 increase ~50–150ms).
B) Force local KV cache warmup / reload for affected boxes (low risk).
C) Temporarily enable per-tenant conservative fallback (route BrightCart to the verified-compact model variant with lower throughput but smaller memory working set). Risk: ~10–15% higher token cost, possible semantic variance.
D) If re-route + cache warmup doesn't help, graceful restart of two problematic hosts (higher risk: short-term increased tail while connections re-establish).

I attached a brief runbook with command snippets. If product approves option C we can toggle it now (per-tenant override exists but needs Product authorization).

Runbook attachment: runbook-mitigations.pdf

Marissa
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Marissa — congrats on the triage. Quick product/infra notes: 

- Option C (per-tenant fallback to verified-compact) is available and is the lowest-lift mitigation. It trades throughput per-request for stability and RAM footprint. Acceptable as a temporary mitigation with customer consent. Rollback is straightforward: toggle per-tenant routing back to the normal model variant.
- We do NOT have a clean on-demand per-tenant qps cap in the console today; that's a product gap. As a stop-gap we can apply a rate limiter at the gateway for BrightCart (SRE + infra work).
- Enabling compact variant will likely increase token unit cost ~12% for BrightCart but will restore throughput within minutes in most cases.

Product asks / decision needed from CS / account owner (Tessa):
1) Approve per-tenant fallback to verified-compact for BrightCart for up to 4 hours while we stabilize.
2) Approve gateway rate-limit cap at 60% of current sustained qps if we see sustained queueing after fallback.
3) Post-incident: prioritize INF-7891 (per-tenant throttles & circuit breakers) on next sprint — this incident underlines the need.

Proposed customer-facing blurb (draft):
"Hi Sarah — we see elevated tail latency and are taking a targeted mitigation that will temporarily route BrightCart to a verified compact model variant to stabilize throughput. You may see slightly different latency characteristics and a small change in per-token usage. We expect a visible improvement within 10–20 minutes. We'll follow up with a full root cause and timeline for permanent remediation"

If CS approves, SRE can flip the per-tenant routing — please confirm and I'll coordinate rollback windows and monitoring queries.

Karthik
Director, Product — Serving Runtime

Sarah — quick update and immediate plan of action from the Redwood side.

Summary:
- We observed the same anomaly in our telemetry for BrightCart in us-west-2 (start ~08:55 PDT). Root cause analysis is ongoing.
- Immediate mitigation we will apply: we will route BrightCart traffic to our verified-compact model variant now. This is a targeted, per-tenant change intended to reduce working set pressure and stabilize throughput.
- Expected customer impact: you should see throughput return toward normal within 10–20 minutes. p95 should drop substantially; some responses may be slightly slower or exhibit minor semantic differences. Per-token billing may increase by ~10–15% while the mitigation is active.

Operational notes / timeline:
- 10:25 — SRE rebalanced traffic away from two hosts showing KV eviction pressure (complete).
- 10:28 — SRE triggered per-tenant routing to verified-compact for BrightCart (in progress).
- 10:45 — We'll give a follow-up update or earlier if we detect regressions.

We own execution and rollback. Next steps: SRE will keep the runbook steps open and provide a postmortem. Product will file INF-7891 to address per-tenant qps/circuit-breaker gaps.

If you prefer not to be routed to compact, tell us and we'll explore an alternate approach (gateway throttling or host restarts), but that may require a short maintenance window.

Apologies for the disruption — we know checkout reliability is high priority. I'll be your point of contact; reply here and we'll keep you updated.

Thanks —
